criticisms.target: the claim that nine model checks amount to only 2.18 independent opinions
criticisms.criticism: The cited 2.18 result comes from specific NLI and reward benchmarks so the work has not shown that the same dependence holds for the open-ended document review workflow it tells readers to measure.

criticisms.target: the claim that adding models stops buying anything after the fifth judge
criticisms.criticism: A diminishing marginal contribution in one nine-model experiment does not establish a general five-model cutoff for different models tasks prompts or error distributions.

criticisms.target: the claim that swapping model families does not fix dependence
criticisms.criticism: A reduction in correlation from roughly 0.67 to 0.53 demonstrates that model-family diversity does add independence so the work must quantify whether that gain is operationally insufficient rather than dismiss it categorically.

criticisms.target: the claim that a second opinion provides almost no benefit except on near-tie decisions
criticisms.criticism: The work must show that the cited verification experiment measures the same kind of checking and decision outcomes as its proposed document-review workflow before transferring the near-zero average effect to this use case.

criticisms.target: the effective-sample-size formula used as the independence test
criticisms.criticism: The work must establish that an equicorrelation effective-sample-size formula designed for correlated samples is valid when its r is derived from agreement among heterogeneous qualitative criticisms rather than a common quantitative outcome.

criticisms.target: the recommendation to treat solo findings as the entire return from multiple checks
criticisms.criticism: A finding raised by only one reviewer can be a unique false positive rather than unique information so the work must measure the precision or validity of solo findings before treating them as the benefit of reviewer diversity.

criticisms.target: the claim that multi-model agreement should not raise confidence
criticisms.criticism: Correlated agreement can still be positive evidence when reviewers have individual accuracy above chance so the work must demonstrate that observed dependence eliminates the likelihood update from agreement rather than merely reducing it.

criticisms.target: the proposed nine-check independence test as an actionable measure
criticisms.criticism: The work must validate that its resulting effective-opinion number predicts downstream error detection decision quality or calibration better than simpler measures before presenting that number as operationally meaningful.
